clue.text: Sailor boy's ticket

explanation.surface: A young sailor's pass for travel.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the light as SEA'S SON: a sailor is a son of the sea. The second is the British commuter's word for a ticket valid for a long period.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor is figuratively a son of the ocean, and a 'season' is short for a season ticket covering months of travel.

clue.text: Two minims may be all you can get in 'a bar

definitions.text: Two minims may be all you can get in 'a bar

parts.words: Two minims may be all you can get in 'a bar
parts.note: a whole note equals two half notes and fills a bar of common time; minims also suggest tiny drinks in a pub bar

explanation.surface: In a pub you may get only a couple of drops.
explanation.walkthrough: A minim is a half note in music and also a tiny liquid measure, so the bar may be a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole note lasts as long as two half notes, filling a four-four bar.

clue.text: Programme terrific? Not entirely, but reflects current trends

indicators.note: only part of these two words is taken, so a run of letters inside them is used

explanation.surface: A great show? Only in part, but it mirrors the fashions of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current trends' look like fashions, but the current is electric.
explanation.definitionFit: This meter measures electrical current in amps, so its reading shows how the flow varies.

clue.text: Speaker swallows one drink for a starter

indicators.note: the word for a speaker takes the other pieces inside it, as a mouth takes a drink

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker
I is the Roman numeral for one
gin is a spirit drink

explanation.surface: A speechmaker downs a drink before the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' looks like the first course, but it means one who starts something.
explanation.definitionFit: One who begins something is its founder or creator.

clue.text: Fought and was thrown out

explanation.surface: Someone had a brawl and was ejected for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrap is to brawl, and something scrapped has been discarded as rubbish.

clue.text: Artist allowed to follow Bible wedding scene

indicators.note: the pieces for allowed and to come after the wedding town

parts.note: Cana in Galilee is where Jesus turned water into wine at a wedding
let means allowed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter permitted to come after a scriptural marriage tableau.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian painter of eighteenth-century city views.

clue.text: In which a babe prepares to do battle ?

definitions.text: In which a babe prepares to do battle ?

parts.words: In which a babe prepares to do battle ?
parts.note: a babe is carried in someone's embrace, and getting ready to fight means taking up weapons

explanation.surface: A baby readies itself for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue fuses 'babe in ...' (a babe carried in the embrace) with 'to ...' meaning prepare for war.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby is held in the limbs of its carrier, and weapons are what a soldier takes up.

clue.text: Bird's milk order-one pound

parts.note: a pinta is British slang for a pint of milk, as ordered from the milkman
I is the Roman numeral for one
L stands for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A bird orders a pint of milk and pays a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-tailed dabbling duck is a kind of waterfowl.

clue.text: Grounds for many regulations

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
regs is short for regulations

explanation.surface: Justification for lots of rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds' looks like reasons, but it means sediment, as in coffee grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment left in a cup or bottle, like coffee grounds.

clue.text: Old port may unfortunately be flat

explanation.surface: An ancient harbour may sadly be lying low.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Phoenician seaport in Lebanon shares its name with a wheel's rubber casing, which may get a puncture.

clue.text: Prepare for the silence of an Egyptian tomb ?

definitions.text: Prepare for the silence of an Egyptian tomb ?

parts.words: Prepare for the silence of an Egyptian tomb ?
parts.note: embalming a body for burial in a pharaoh's tomb, read also as making someone 'mum', that is silent

explanation.surface: Getting ready for eternal quiet in a pyramid.
explanation.walkthrough: MUM means silent, so the verb reads as 'make mum', besides its sense of embalming a corpse in the Egyptian manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Egyptians embalmed and wrapped corpses before entombing them.

clue.text: Man appointed is possibly one without a source of wealth

definitions.text: possibly one without a source of wealth

explanation.surface: A nominated candidate may turn out to be penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the light as NO MINE plus the suffix -EE: one who has no mine, the classic source of riches.
explanation.definitionFit: A person named for an office is the one put forward; split up, the word suggests someone with no gold mine.

clue.text: He painted one small room in Tobit (RV)

indicators.note: RV stands for Revised Version, so the book's name is to be revised, that is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Renaissance painter depicted a little chamber in the Apocrypha's Book of Tobit, Revised Version.
explanation.walkthrough: '(RV)' looks like a Bible reference but is the anagram signal: TOBIT revised gives BOTTI, then CELL and I follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florentine painter of the Birth of Venus is a man, so 'He' stands for him; the clue says he painted.

clue.text: Crazy cricketers

explanation.surface: Madcap players of cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone batty is mad, and in cricket the batsmen are called bats.

clue.text: Vehicular ecstasies ?

parts.note: delights or raptures, read also as means of conveyance such as buses and lorries

explanation.surface: The thrills of motoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Raptures carry a person away, and vehicles carry goods and people.

clue.text: 'ow Brutus introduces the next speaker-put on one side

explanation.surface: In Julius Caesar, Brutus hands the platform to the following orator before stepping aside.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Julius Caesar, Brutus tells the crowd to listen to Mark Antony; dropping the H in Cockney style gives 'ear Mark'. The second sense means set aside for a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve funds for a particular use is to set them apart; the first part is a dropped-H 'hear Mark'.

clue.text: X plays on ice. Finds things somewhat hairy

parts.note: X written at the end of a letter stands for a kiss
to curl is to play the Scottish game of curling on ice

explanation.surface: Someone plays an ice sport and has close shaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Curling is a game of sliding stones on ice. The answer names small curls of hair pressed flat on the forehead.
explanation.definitionFit: Small flat curls of hair worn on the forehead or temple.

clue.text: Diminutive demi-mondaine's bonne-bouche

parts.note: a demi-mondaine is a woman of loose morals, a tart in slang
-LET is a suffix making small things, as in booklet or piglet

explanation.surface: A small courtesan's tasty morsel, in a string of French borrowings.
explanation.walkthrough: A bonne-bouche is French for a tasty titbit.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pastry with a filling is a dainty mouthful, which is what the French phrase means.

clue.text: Russian newsmen hold inscription slab to be in poor form

indicators.note: the agency's name holds the slab's word inside it

parts.note: Tass was the Soviet news agency
a stele is an upright stone slab bearing an inscription

explanation.surface: Soviet journalists keep a carved stone to look bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking refinement, vulgar or in bad taste.

clue.text: Green ruined, no use-contains 'doodlebug

indicators.note: the scrambled letters hold the other piece inside them
something ruined is wrecked, so the letters of these words are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the doodlebug was the German V1 flying bomb of the Second World War, read as the letters VI

explanation.surface: Something green and spoiled is no good, with a beetle inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' turns NO USE into ENOUS, and 'contains' puts VI (the V1 flying bomb) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Green with envy is the idiom for jealousy, so green means jealous.

clue.text: Morally good? No, but as good as the real thing

definitions.text: Morally good? No, but as good as the real thing

parts.words: Morally good? No, but as good as the real thing
parts.note: not the word for virtuous, which looks similar, but its near-twin meaning effective in practice though not in name

explanation.surface: Not righteous, but just as effective as the genuine article.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening invites the word for morally good, which shares its start with the answer; the rest gives the real sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something effectively so in practice, though not formally or physically, is in effect the same.

clue.text: .Comprehensive edition 14 us all

explanation.surface: A complete volume that carries everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 refers to the answer at 14 down, TRANSPORTS: a bus transports us all, and the Latin word means 'for all'.
explanation.definitionFit: A collected volume gathers several works into one book, and the old name for a bus means 'for everyone' in Latin.

clue.text: Marie Antoinette's cake

parts.note: the French queen supposedly said that the starving poor should eat a rich bread, usually translated as 'let them eat cake'

explanation.surface: The French queen's famous dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: The French queen's legendary remark named an enriched sweet bun, rendered in English as 'cake'.

clue.text: Shakespeare's far from colourful backing

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for dull is read from its end

parts.note: drab means dull and lacking colour

explanation.surface: Shakespeare had a dull financial sponsor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support, but it turns DRAB round.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare is called the Bard of Avon, a poet.

clue.text: Cambridge players practising punting here ?

explanation.surface: Cambridge sportsmen practising on a punt.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cambridge, the Backs are the college lawns along the River Cam, where people punt. In rugby, the backs are players behind the scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby players behind the scrum are so named, and the riverside lawns of Cambridge colleges bear the name.

clue.text: Comic place for reforming a junior criminal

indicators.note: reforming means forming anew, so these letters are reshaped into the answer

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A funny venue meant to straighten out young offenders.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner in crime who helps the main offender plays the lesser role.

clue.text: Fairy tale's beginning shows it's unique

explanation.surface: The opening of a fairy story shows it happens just one time.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairy stories begin 'upon a time' with this word, which also means on one occasion only.

clue.text: Record one caught — a heroic tale

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A recording with one catch tells a story of heroes.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrative poem of heroic deeds, like the Iliad.

clue.text: King Charles had superior (if equine) hindquarters

parts.note: CR stands for Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles
upper means higher or superior

explanation.surface: A Stuart monarch had a fine rear end, if he were a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The '(if equine)' tells the solver the rump in question is a horse's.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a horse's rump as well as the strap under the tail of a harness.

clue.text: Old Welsh craft takes care of people (about 50)

parts.note: c/o, written CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of

indicators.note: the word for people goes round the numeral, around it

parts.note: a race is a people or nation
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An old Welsh craftsman looks after some fifty people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like a skill, but it is a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round wicker boat covered with hide, traditionally used on Welsh rivers.

clue.text: Miss Cole's terrible faux pas

indicators.note: something terrible is a mess, so the letters of these words are jumbled

parts.note: the name taken as written, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: A young woman named Cole commits an awful social blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical blunder or breach of etiquette is a gaffe.

clue.text: Useful things put in a ship

indicators.note: the word for put sits inside the ship's abbreviation

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
set means put or placed

explanation.surface: Handy items are placed aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Valuable possessions or qualities are resources of benefit.
